Europe PMC: (pamiparib OR "BGB-290") AND ("first-in-human" OR "phase 1" OR "phase I" OR "dose-escalation")
Europe PMC: ("PARPi-7" OR "PARPi7") AND (BrighTNess OR veliparib OR "I-SPY") -- no PARPi-7 test in BrighTNess found
Europe PMC: "BRCA1ness" AND (veliparib OR BrighTNess OR "I-SPY 2")
Europe PMC: ("2X-121" OR E7449) AND breast -- no breast phase 2 paper found
Europe PMC: veliparib AND breast AND ("patient-derived xenograft" OR PDX OR organoid* OR "ex vivo") AND (patient OR clinical) AND (respon* OR correlat* OR predict*)

Full texts read (Europe PMC XML): PMC5572474 Wolf 2017, PMC4747407 McGonigle 2015, PMC7434893 Plummer 2020, PMC7350150 Xiong 2020, PMC13522806 Bui 2026, PMC8854719 Lickliter 2022; abstracts: Daemen 2012, Severson 2017, Wang 2020, Tovey 2023

ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 results-posting dates: NCT01042379 (I-SPY 2, none), NCT03562832 (2X-121 breast, completed 2024-08, none), NCT03575065 (pamiparib breast, 2022-09-07), NCT02032277 (BrighTNess, none), NCT01618136 (E7449 phase 1, none), NCT02361723 (pamiparib phase 1A/1B, none)

added_models.model: I-SPY 2 pre-specified DNA-repair-deficiency expression signatures: PARPi-7 (7 genes, from olaparib sensitivity in 22 breast cancer cell lines) and BRCA1ness (77-gene BRCA1-like classifier)

efficacy.note: PARPi-7 derived from olaparib dose-response in 22 breast cancer cell lines; predicted 8-21% of invasive breast cancers responsive; no patient test yet.
efficacy.quote: Our studies support clinical evaluation of the utility of our seven-gene signature as a predictor of response to olaparib.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry: the signature was built on olaparib, a sibling PARP1/2 inhibitor, so product_in_model is false; BRCA1ness (Severson 2017) joins the same track as a second pre-specified signature tested in the same arm.
efficacy.population: Breast cancer cell lines (n=22) and 1,846 invasive breast cancer expression profiles

efficacy.note: I-SPY 2: pre-specified PARPi-7 and BRCA1ness predicted pCR in the veliparib-carboplatin arm but not in controls; biomarker-by-treatment interaction p<0.05.
efficacy.short: Signatures predicted VC pCR, not control
efficacy.quote: PARPi-7, BRCA1ness, and MP1/2 specifically associated with response in the VC arm but not the control arm.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5572474). n=116 (VC 72, control 44); the arm added carboplatin, which these HRD signatures may also predict, and Wolf 2017 itself defers testing against carboplatin alone.
efficacy.reason: Signature-high pCR rose in VC arm only
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level prediction tested prospectively (pre-specified qualifying-biomarker evaluation), so not a retrodiction; same, direction_only. The carboplatin confound the checker raised on efficacy[2] applies here too (rule question 1): I score the stated interaction as a match and carry the confound in confidence. BrighTNess (Geyer 2022) later showed carboplatin, not veliparib, drove outcome, but no signature test in BrighTNess was found, so the track is not turned.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: pCR rate in signature-positive vs signature-negative patients within the VC arm vs the control arm; the model predicted no effect size
efficacy.population: HER2-negative stage II/III breast cancer, I-SPY 2 veliparib-carboplatin arm and concurrent controls (n=116), NCT01042379

patient_trials.quote: In the I-SPY 2 neoadjuvant setting the BRCA1ness signature associated significantly with response to V-C (p = 0.03), but not in the control arm (p = 0.45).

added_models.model: 2X-121 (E7449) BRCA-deficient xenografts: single-agent MDA-MB-436 (BRCA1-mutant TNBC) with tumour PAR pharmacodynamics, plus MX-1 carboplatin and temozolomide potentiation

engagement.note: Single-dose E7449 100 mg/kg suppressed tumour PAR for 12 h in MDA-MB-436 xenografts, recovering by 24 h; no human PD yet.
engagement.short: Tumour PAR suppressed 12 h in mice
engagement.quote: Treatment with E7449 at 100 mg/kg resulted in significant PARP inhibition that was sustained for at least 12 hours and recovered to basal levels within 24 hours
engagement.judgement: Opening entry for a member drug's own model, which the draft had no track for; MX-1 chemopotentiation by E7449 is folded in as the same xenograft programme.
engagement.population: MDA-MB-436 BRCA1-mutant TNBC xenografts in mice

engagement.note: Phase 1: PAR in PBMCs fell dose-dependently, ~90% at 600 mg QD and at least 70% at 24 h, the readout the xenograft work used.
engagement.quote: PARP inhibition was sustained with a ≥ 70% decrease in PAR levels at 24-h post-dose time points (cycle 1, days 1, 7, 8 and 16 [at 0 h for each]).
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC7434893). PBMC, not tumour, PAR in patients; mixed solid tumours (4 breast), allowed for engagement.
engagement.reason: PAR fell in patients as in mice
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Plummer cites the xenograft PD but states no side-by-side comparison. Direction only, since matrices differ (mouse tumour vs human PBMC) and no fold is compared.
engagement.magnitude_basis: PAR suppression over the dosing interval: mouse tumour (12 h at 100 mg/kg) vs patient PBMC (at least 70% at 24 h, 600 mg QD)
engagement.population: Advanced solid tumours, mixed (n=41; breast 4, gBRCA 6), NCT01618136

dose.note: MDA-MB-436: 30 or 100 mg/kg once daily for 28 days gave significant antitumour activity and was well tolerated; no human exposure yet.
dose.quote: In an in vivo subcutaneous MDA-MB-436 xenograft model, administration of E7449 at 30 or 100 mg/kg once daily for 28 days resulted in statistically significant antitumor activity
dose.confidence_note: Full text read; mouse plasma exposure is not reported, so the dose target is the PD-active regimen, not an AUC.
dose.judgement: Opening entry; the model's dose claim is a tolerated PD-active once-daily regimen (tolerability 'data not shown').
dose.population: MDA-MB-436 BRCA1-mutant TNBC xenografts in mice

dose.note: 600 mg once daily was the MTD and RP2D, giving maximal, sustained PAR inhibition; the model's tolerated PD-active regimen was reached.
dose.quote: Maximal inhibition was achieved at the MTD (600 mg once daily)
dose.confidence_note: Full text read. Mouse tolerability was 'data not shown' and no exposure bridge exists, so the margin call rests on a qualitative statement; fatigue DLTs appeared one step above the PD-saturating dose.
dose.judgement: Paired by me. Decision 16: the model stated 30-100 mg/kg was effective and well tolerated, and patients reached the PD-saturating dose without a blocking toxicity, so same with margin_stated true. Whether it was enough is open: breast efficacy is unreported (NCT03562832), so no derived status.
dose.magnitude_basis: PD-active regimen reached (PAR inhibition ~90% at 600 mg QD); no mouse exposure to compare

efficacy.note: E7449 alone shrank BRCA-deficient xenografts (MDA-MB-436) and potentiated carboplatin and temozolomide in MX-1; no breast patient comparison exists.
efficacy.quote: Chemotherapy was potentiated by E7449 and single agent had significant antitumor activity in BRCA-deficient xenografts.
efficacy.judgement: Untested, not contra: Plummer 2020's two gBRCA breast patients progressed, but in a mixed dose-escalation (50-800 mg) with n=2 that is not an admissible efficacy test; the DRP-selected breast phase 2 (NCT03562832, completed 2024-08) has no results or paper. The DRP itself is the draft's separate 2x121-drp-in-silico track.
efficacy.population: MDA-MB-436 and MX-1 BRCA-deficient breast xenografts in mice

patient_trials.quote: partial response in 1 patient (high-grade serous ovarian tumours) and progressive disease in 3 patients (2 breast tumours and 1 ovarian tumour).

safety.note: Model stated no toxicity at effective doses and, specifically, none of the intestinal toxicity seen with other tankyrase inhibitors.
safety.quote: Particularly noteworthy was the lack of toxicity, most significantly the lack of intestinal toxicity reported for other TNKS inhibitors.
safety.confidence_note: Full text read; toxicity judged on body weight and deaths, no haematology or histology reported.
safety.judgement: A stated prediction (no intestinal toxicity) that a mouse could test, so it is scoreable once patients are dosed.
safety.population: MDA-MB-436 and MX-1 xenografts in mice

safety.note: Phase 1: no intestinal DLTs; diarrhoea 29% any grade; DLTs were fatigue and anaphylaxis, with unexpected rash, photosensitivity and chromaturia.
safety.quote: Thirty-nine patients (95.1%) in the dose-escalation cohort had treatment-related AEs, with the most common being fatigue (63%), chromaturia (49%), nausea (34%), diarrhoea (29%), maculopapular rash (27%), photosensitivity reaction (24%) and decreased appetite (24%)
safety.confidence_note: Full text read. Mixed solid-tumour phase 1 (imported); the model's stated prediction concerned tankyrase-type intestinal toxicity, and the trial reports no intestinal DLT, but 29% any-grade diarrhoea and unforeseen cutaneous AEs make this a partial hold.
safety.judgement: Paired by me. The stated prediction (no TNKS-type intestinal toxicity) held: no intestinal DLT and the dose-limiting harms were fatigue and one anaphylaxis. Rash, photosensitivity and chromaturia were unpredicted, but an efficacy xenograft study does not assess skin or urine, so not askable silence; source_calls_it partial.
safety.magnitude_basis: Presence of intestinal toxicity: none dose-limiting in patients vs none in mice

added_models.model: Pamiparib's own BRCA1-mutant MDA-MB-436 TNBC xenograft with tumour PAR pharmacodynamics and a mouse PK/PD model (head-to-head vs olaparib)

engagement.note: Tumour PAR inhibition in MDA-MB-436 xenografts tracked plasma and tumour pamiparib dose-proportionally (0.17-10.9 mg/kg); no human PD yet.
engagement.quote: The concentration of pamiparib in serum or at the tumor site increased proportionally with dose and positively correlated with the extent of PAR inhibition in tumors
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC7350150). Publication (2020) postdates the phase 1 start (2015); the model predates its paper, so the opening year is a proxy.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry for pamiparib's own model, which the draft scores only on the olaparib GEMM; a different system (xenograft, product dosed) with its own PK/PD, so its own track.
engagement.population: MDA-MB-436 BRCA1-mutant TNBC xenografts in BALB/c nude mice

engagement.note: Phase 1A/1B: PBMC PAR inhibition rose with dose to 10 mg BID and plateaued near 80% at or above it.
engagement.quote: There was a dose-dependent increase in PAR inhibition in PBMCs from 2.5 mg to 10 mg BID; the inhibition was sustained at approximately 80% at pamiparib doses of 10 mg BID or higher
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC8854719). PBMC not tumour PAR; mixed solid tumours (55% ovarian, 7% breast), allowed for engagement.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Lickliter cites the xenograft PARylation data but states no side-by-side comparison; direction only.
engagement.magnitude_basis: Dose-dependent PAR inhibition: mouse tumour vs patient PBMC; no fold compared

dose.note: MDA-MB-436: pamiparib 1.6-12.5 mg/kg BID for 28 days regressed every tumour with no body-weight effect; mouse AUC/dose 552 ng·h/mL per mg/kg.
dose.quote: In comparisons of efficacy, pamiparib induced tumor regression on day 29, resulting in 100% objective responses at the lowest dose (1.6 mg/kg).
dose.confidence_note: Full text read; the paper's PK/PD model links dose to PAR inhibition but states no human target exposure.
dose.judgement: Opening entry; the stated tolerated effective dose (no body-weight effect at all efficacious doses) is the margin that decision 16 scores.

dose.note: RP2D 60 mg BID (MTD 80 mg BID) sits well above the 10 mg BID PAR-inhibition plateau, so the PD target was reached with margin.
dose.quote: MTD was 80 mg BID and RP2D was 60 mg BID.
dose.confidence_note: Full text read. No exposure bridge from mouse AUC to human AUC was computed by either source; magnitude is direction only.
dose.judgement: Paired by me. The model stated its efficacious doses were tolerated (no body-weight effect) and patients reached PAR-saturating exposure six-fold below the RP2D without a blocking toxicity: same, margin_stated true. Enough: EOC ORR 41% in the same study and gBRCA breast ORR 38-62% (Xu 2023) followed.
dose.magnitude_basis: PAR-inhibition plateau (10 mg BID) vs RP2D (60 mg BID) and MTD (80 mg BID); no AUC comparison

efficacy.note: Pamiparib alone regressed BRCA1-mutant MDA-MB-436 xenografts at every dose, 16-fold more potent than olaparib; BRCA-wild-type MDA-MB-231 cells resistant.
efficacy.quote: Pamiparib has good bioavailability and is 16-fold more potent than olaparib in an efficacy study using BRCA1 mutated MDA-MB-436 breast cancer xenograft model.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry: genotype-selected single-agent activity is a patient-level prediction, distinct from the draft's olaparib GEMM track in model and in drug dosed.
efficacy.population: MDA-MB-436 BRCA1-mutant TNBC xenografts in mice

efficacy.note: Pamiparib monotherapy phase 2 (China): ORR 38% in gBRCA TNBC and 62% in gBRCA HR+/HER2-, as the BRCA1-mutant xenograft predicted.
efficacy.quote: In the TNBC cohort, ORR was 38.2% (95% confidence interval [CI] 25.4-52.3) and median duration of response (DoR) was 7.0 months (95% CI 3.9-not estimable).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (the draft's efficacy[7] verified the quote and dates); single-arm phase 2, no comparator.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: Xu 2023 cites the preclinical package but states no comparison. Same, direction only; the same trial also sits on the olaparib GEMM track, which is a different system, so both tracks score it. Year 2022 from registry results posting (2022-09-07), before epub (2022-12-02).
efficacy.magnitude_basis: Objective response in gBRCA breast cancer vs 100% regression in the BRCA1-mutant xenograft; no human effect size predicted
efficacy.population: gBRCA1/2-mutated HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (China), NCT03575065

safety.note: Xenograft study reported no effect on body weight at any dose; haematology not measured; no patient comparison yet.
safety.quote: all treatments had no effect on mouse body weight
safety.confidence_note: Full text read; body weight was the only toxicity readout reported.
safety.judgement: Opening entry; tolerability stated on body weight alone, so the haematology question is askable silence (checker rule question 2 is open).

safety.note: Pamiparib monotherapy in gBRCA breast cancer: haematologic grade 3+ TEAEs common, 65% dose-reduced; the mouse that could show cytopenias reported none.
safety.quote: The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), treatment-related TEAEs, and ≥ Grade 3 TEAEs were hematologic (including anemia, decreased neutrophil count, and decreased white blood cell count).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level on the patient side. Same logic and same open rule question as the draft's safety[2]; Lickliter 2022 (mixed tumours) had already shown grade 3 or worse anaemia in 24.8% in 2021.
safety.judgement: Paired by me. A mouse can show marrow suppression and the study measured only body weight, so its 'no effect' is askable silence contradicted by patients; counted here, not in dose, because the model never predicted the harm (decision 16). Low confidence pending rule question 2.
safety.population: gBRCA1/2-mutated HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (China), NCT03575065

added_models.model: Patient-derived TNBC organoids (n=14) tested for veliparib-cisplatin response against an I-SPY 2-trained classifier (PARPi7 plus lymphocyte signature)

efficacy.note: Classifier trained on I-SPY 2 VC-arm pCR (PARPi7, LYMPHS; AUC 0.91) applied to 14 TNBC organoids: 7 predicted sensitive, 5 intermediate, 2 resistant.
efficacy.quote: The area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve for the model using PARPi7 and LYMPHS_PCA to predict the probability of pCR to veliparib-carboplatin in patients with TNBC was 0.912
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC13522806). Opening entry in the same year as the comparison, as the system was built and tested in one paper.
efficacy.judgement: A distinct ex-vivo system (patient-derived organoids) built after I-SPY 2, BrighTNess and Geyer 2022 were known, so any match is a retrodiction.

efficacy.note: Organoid veliparib-cisplatin responses were mostly concordant with the patient-trained predictions; the sensitive line responded to cisplatin with or without veliparib.
efficacy.quote: the response patterns of most organoids were generally concordant with model predictions, with predicted sensitive organoids demonstrating greater treatment response than predicted resistant organoids in the majority of cases
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. Four organoids tested in depth; concordance is with a patient-data classifier, not with each donor's own clinical outcome; veliparib added nothing over cisplatin in the sensitive line, echoing BrighTNess.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: built 2026 after the VC-arm pCR, BrighTNess and Geyer 2022 were known, so retro not same (decision 10). source_calls_it partial because the source says most, not all. Comparison stated: the paper itself puts organoid response beside patient-derived predictions. Not a prospective test of patient selection.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: Rank of organoid veliparib-cisplatin sensitivity vs classifier-predicted sensitivity class
efficacy.population: TNBC patient-derived organoids (n=14, 4 tested in depth) vs I-SPY 2 veliparib-carboplatin-arm TNBC patients

considered_not_added: Kummar 2009 mouse PK/PD target (0.21 umol/L plasma from single-dose PAR studies): a stated comparison on the existing mx1-brca-xenograft-chemopotentiation track (set comparison_stated true there), not a new system.
2X-121 drug-response predictor (DRP, Plummer 2020): already the draft's 2x121-drp-in-silico track; the breast phase 2 it selected for (NCT03562832) completed 2024-08 with no results or paper found.

Severson 2017 BRCA1ness signature in I-SPY 2: same pre-specified signature set and same arm as Wolf 2017, so folded into ispy2-parpi7-brca1ness-signatures as a patient_trials record rather than a separate track.
Myriad HRD / genomic-scar scores and gBRCA status in BrighTNess and I-SPY 2: tumour genomic assays, not model systems with a model-side prediction (Wolf 2017 explicitly did not test them); no track.

TNT trial signature analysis (Tovey 2023): tests PARPi-7-type DDR signatures against carboplatin vs docetaxel, no member drug, so it cannot score; it only bears on the carboplatin confound noted on the signature track.
I-SPY 2 durvalumab/olaparib/paclitaxel arm (Pusztai 2021): olaparib is not a member of this tile's class.
Lickliter 2022 TNBC expansion arm (Arm 2): antitumour activity was not assessed individually, so no breast efficacy comparison for pamiparib's own model beyond Xu 2023.
Xiong 2020 intracranial H209 + temozolomide model and Wang 2020 brain-penetration DMPK: SCLC-brain and glioma predictions (tested in Schiff 2026, Piotrowski 2025), outside the breast context.
Veliparib population-PK or exposure-response models for dose selection: not searched within the budget; no in-silico dose model for breast cancer surfaced in the searches run.
Patient-derived xenograft co-clinical trials with a member drug in breast cancer: the Europe PMC PDX/organoid search returned only Bui 2026 (added) and reviews.
